facts.statement: Aralazhdarcho was an azhdarchid pterosaur that lived in Kazakhstan during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Aralazhdarcho is a genus of azhdarchid pterosaur that lived during the Santonian to the early Campanian ages of the Late Cretaceous period in what is now Kazakhstan.

facts.statement: The only known species is Aralazhdarcho bostobensis, which was named and described by Alexander Averianov.
facts.quote: The type and only known species is Aralazhdarcho bostobensis, named and described by Russian paleontologist Alexander Averianov.

facts.statement: Fossils of Aralazhdarcho were discovered in the Bostobe Formation of Kazakhstan.
facts.quote: Its remains were found in the Bostobe Formation of Kazakhstan.

facts.statement: The genus and species were formally named in 2007 by Alexander Averianov.
facts.quote: Aralazhdarcho bostobensis as a genus and type species was named in 2007 by Russian paleontologist Alexander Averianov.

facts.statement: The name combines the Aral Sea and the genus Azhdarcho, while the species name refers to the Bostobe Formation.
facts.quote: The generic name Aralazhdarcho is derived from the Aral Sea and the related genus Azhdarcho, while the specific name bostobensis refers to its provenance from the Bostobe Formation.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of the front part of a neck vertebra, likely the fifth or sixth one.
facts.quote: Aralazhdarcho is based on holotype ZIN PH, no. 9/43, consisting of the anterior end of a neck vertebra, probably the fifth or sixth.

facts.statement: The fossils were found at the Shakh-Shakh locality in Kazakhstan.
facts.quote: The remains were found at the Shakh-Shakh locality of Kazakhstan.

facts.statement: It is classified in the family Azhdarchidae because it lacks teeth and dates to the correct geological period.
facts.quote: Due to its toothless anatomy and the geological age of its fossil remains, Aralazhdarcho was assigned to the family Azhdarchidae.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the genus Samrukia is actually a junior synonym of Aralazhdarcho.
facts.quote: The pterosaur genus Samrukia has been speculated to be a junior synonym of Aralazhdarcho.

facts.statement: Some analyses place Aralazhdarcho in the subfamily Quetzalcoatlinae alongside Phosphatodraco.
facts.quote: The first one is by American paleontologist Brian Andres, in which he found Aralazhdarcho within the subfamily Quetzalcoatlinae, in a basal (primitive) clade with Phosphatodraco from Morocco.

facts.statement: Other studies suggest Aralazhdarcho belongs outside the Quetzalcoatlinae subfamily in a more basal position.
facts.quote: However, contrary to Andres in 2021, Pêgas and colleagues recovered Aralazhdarcho outside Quetzalcoatlinae in a more basal position within Azhdarchidae.

facts.statement: This pterosaur lived during the Santonian or early Campanian stages of the Late Cretaceous in Kazakhstan.
facts.quote: Aralazhdarcho es un género de pterosaurio azdárquido del Santoniense o principios del Campaniano (Cretácico Superior) de Kazajistán.

facts.statement: The animal lived between 85.7 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Campanian (85.7 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The family classification for this genus is Azhdarchidae.
Averianov assigned it to Azhdarchidae based on its lack of teeth and geological age.
facts.quote: Aralazhdarchofue asignado por Averianov a la familia Azhdarchidae, en vista de su carencia de dientes y su edad geológica.

rejected.statement: The holotype specimen was originally described in 2004 before the genus was named in 2007.
rejected.quote: However, the holotype specimen had already been described back in 2004.

rejected.statement: Paratype fossils include a cheekbone, a toothless jaw fragment, vertebrae, a scapula, a wing finger bone, and a femur.
rejected.quote: Several paratypes have also been referred: a jugal, a toothless lower jaw fragment, centra from vertebrae, the distal end of a scapula, the proximal end of a second phalanx of the left wing finger and the proximal end of a left femur.
